item.text: {"question_id":"7B.7","answer":"During 2023, the record shows mixed but materially adverse accountability conduct. López Obrador issued orders and supported investigative mechanisms for Ayotzinapa, and authorities made documented agreements with the GIEI, pursued some arrests and prosecutions, and supplied evidence for CNDH follow-up; these actions show partial cooperation rather than blanket noncompliance (BATCH-0003-E016; BATCH-0004-E012; BATCH-0004-E013; BATCH-0013-E001; BATCH-0013-E004; BATCH-0021-R01-E009). However, SEDENA refused to provide records covered by the president’s order, while independent investigators reported withheld evidence and ultimately could not continue; the supplied material does not establish that López Obrador personally ordered each concealment, but it does document his failure to compel cooperation after scrutiny reached the military and his defense of the military’s role (BATCH-0003-E015; BATCH-0003-E016; BATCH-0004-E013). The accountability environment was further weakened by López Obrador’s veto of INAI commissioner appointments, coalition-backed proposals to eliminate the agency, and a substantially repeated national-security secrecy order after the Supreme Court overturned an earlier one (BATCH-0047-E013; BATCH-0026-E020). He also publicly denied or minimized spyware allegations, while INAI orders concerning SEDENA’s Pegasus contracts remained unfulfilled during the period (BATCH-0026-E019; BATCH-0014-E006). Public attacks, disclosure of journalists’ personal information, and the absence of a sanction after an INAI finding concerning López Obrador’s disclosure are directly attributable adverse conduct, although the supplied evidence does not establish that every related legal action was retaliatory or illegitimate (BATCH-0031-E010). Overall, the evidence supports documented presidential obstruction or weakening of independent scrutiny in specific matters, alongside partial cooperation and enforcement; it does not prove a personal command for all institutional concealment or a universal pattern across every accountability process.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0004-E013","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0026-E019","BATCH-0014-E006","BATCH-0031-E010"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0004-E012","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0013-E004","BATCH-0021-R01-E009","BATCH-0026-E020"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence is concentrated on Ayotzinapa, transparency institutions, spyware, and press-related scrutiny rather than a comprehensive record of subpoenas, judgments, audits, pardons, or disclosure duties.","Military noncompliance and some agency or legislative failures are not fully linked to López Obrador’s knowledge, intent, or action after notice.","Several adverse claims are investigative or evaluative reports rather than final judicial findings; the evidence does not establish personal command for every concealed or surveilled act.","Some favorable material records agreements, orders, prosecutions, or documentary cooperation, but not complete implementation or successful remedies."],"corrections_made":["Replaced the draft’s broad claim of institutional obstruction or tolerance with a narrower conclusion tied to specifically documented presidential actions and responses.","Separated SEDENA and legislative or agency noncompliance from López Obrador’s personal attribution, knowledge, and failure to compel cooperation.","Corrected the treatment of INAI’s quorum crisis by distinguishing the president’s vetoes and dissolution proposals from Senate appointment failures and later Supreme Court restoration.","Added and strengthened contrary evidence concerning GIEI agreements, government orders, prosecutions, CNDH follow-up, and other cooperation.","Preserved uncertainty around allegations, motive, final findings, and whether conduct was personally commanded or retaliatory."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Reopen if final judicial findings, complete INAI appointment and complaint outcomes, or direct records of presidential instructions and enforcement become available.","Reopen if additional evidence covers subpoenas, judgments, audits, pardons, disclosure compliance, or retaliation beyond the supplied themes."]}
